content.text: Evidence clearly favors KB-002: coolant_temp_c rises steadily and sustained from 89°C baseline to 114°C over ~90 minutes, with coolant_level_pct falling in lockstep from 96% to 76% — a genuine progressive correlation, not a transient blip. This rules out KB-001 (sensor glitch), which would show an isolated spike with no coolant level change. Oil pressure and RPM remain stable/normal, consistent with a coolant leak rather than broader engine failure.

input.description: KB search returned two conflicting entries: KB-001 attributes coolant spikes to a transient sensor calibration glitch (fix: restart_sensor), while KB-002 attributes sustained spikes correlated with falling coolant level to an actual leak (fix: schedule_service_visit). Telemetry shows a steady, sustained rise in coolant_temp_c from ~89°C to 114°C over 90 minutes, tracking in lockstep with coolant_level_pct dropping from 96% to 76% -- not an isolated transient reading. This matches KB-002's pattern exactly and rules out KB-001, since a sensor glitch would not correlate with a real drop in coolant level. Oil pressure and RPM stayed normal/stable, pointing specifically to coolant loss rather than a broader mechanical issue. Recommend a physical inspection/service visit to locate and repair the leak.
